findings.title: Error container conditionally inserted — role="alert" may not fire in VoiceOver
findings.description: When error transitions from empty to populated, the component removes the non-error slot element and inserts a new <div role="alert"> node. VoiceOver on macOS requires the live region container to pre-exist in the DOM; a newly inserted role="alert" node does not reliably trigger an announcement.
findings.fix: Replace the conditional role="alert" div with a persistent <div id=${this._errorId} role="alert" aria-live="assertive"> always present in the DOM. Populate it conditionally with error text; leave it empty (not removed) when no error exists.

findings.title: Missing aria-required on native input
findings.description: The native <input> uses the boolean ?required attribute for constraint validation but does not set aria-required="true". Some screen reader / browser combinations (notably JAWS with Firefox) do not expose the native required attribute via the accessibility tree when it lives inside a shadow root. aria-required is the reliable cross-AT mechanism.
findings.fix: Add aria-required=${this.required ? 'true' : nothing} alongside the existing ?required=${this.required} on the native <input>.

findings.title: Missing delegatesFocus: true in shadowRootOptions
findings.description: The component uses a manual focus() override to delegate focus to the inner input. Without delegatesFocus: true, clicking the shadow host in certain browser/AT combinations may not correctly route focus to the inner input, and the :focus pseudo-class on the host is not automatically set when the inner input is focused.
findings.fix: Add static override shadowRootOptions = { ...LitElement.shadowRootOptions, delegatesFocus: true } to the HelixTextInput class.

findings.title: Character counter aria-live fires on every keystroke and is also included in aria-describedby
findings.description: The visible counter <div> has aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true", so every character change announces the updated count. The same element's ID is included in aria-describedby, causing it to be read as the textarea description on focus. This creates double-announcement: the counter fires live updates on each keystroke AND is read when the textarea receives focus. On JAWS and NVDA this verbosity can obscure other important announcements. A separate debounced sr-only region already handles the polite live announcement.
findings.fix: Remove aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="true" from the visible counter div. The existing debounced sr-only live region handles the announcement. The counter ID may remain in aria-describedby for on-demand access via virtual cursor, but only the sr-only region should carry aria-live.

findings.title: Error container role="alert" conditionally inserted — may not announce in VoiceOver
findings.description: Identical to B2-001: the error <div role="alert"> is conditionally inserted/removed rather than kept as a persistent live region. VoiceOver on macOS requires the live region container to pre-exist in the DOM before text is populated.
findings.fix: Use a persistent <div role="alert" aria-live="assertive"> always in the DOM, populated conditionally with error text rather than inserted/removed.

findings.title: Missing aria-required on native textarea
findings.description: The native <textarea> has ?required but no aria-required="true". Same shadow DOM AT reliability issue as hx-text-input.
findings.fix: Add aria-required=${this.required ? 'true' : nothing} to the native <textarea> element.

findings.title: Missing delegatesFocus: true in shadowRootOptions
findings.description: Same as B2-003. hx-textarea uses a manual focus() override without delegatesFocus: true. All form input components should use the declarative focus delegation API.
findings.fix: Add static override shadowRootOptions = { ...LitElement.shadowRootOptions, delegatesFocus: true } to the HelixTextarea class.

findings.title: Slotted error creates broken aria-describedby reference
findings.description: When the error slot is used without the error property, hasError becomes true and aria-describedby is set to include this._errorId. However, the shadow DOM element with that ID only renders when this.error prop is truthy — not when only slot content is present. The native input has an aria-describedby pointing to a non-existent element ID. Screen readers silently ignore broken IDREFs, meaning the slotted error is not announced to assistive technology.
findings.fix: Render the error container element (with id=${this._errorId}) whenever hasError is true — both when this.error prop is set and when this._hasErrorSlot is true. Place the <slot name="error"> inside this always-rendered container so the IDREF is always valid.

findings.title: Stepper buttons have tabindex="-1" — not reachable by keyboard
findings.description: The increment and decrement buttons have tabindex="-1", removing them from the sequential keyboard tab order. While ArrowUp/ArrowDown on the input provides stepping, this is not disclosed to assistive technology and is not discoverable by keyboard-only users. WCAG 2.1.1 requires that all functionality is available from a keyboard.
findings.fix: Either: (a) remove tabindex="-1" from stepper buttons so keyboard users can tab to them; or (b) keep tabindex="-1" but add aria-keyshortcuts="ArrowUp ArrowDown" to the input and document the keyboard pattern in aria-describedby.

findings.title: Error message inside slot fallback — role="alert" insertion may not fire
findings.description: The error div (role="alert") is nested as fallback content inside a <slot name="error"> and the entire slot+error block is conditionally swapped. VoiceOver on macOS requires the alert container to pre-exist in the DOM before text is inserted.
findings.fix: Move the error container outside the slot: always render <div id=${this._errorId} role="alert" aria-live="assertive"> in the DOM, populate it with error text conditionally, and keep <slot name="error"> separate for slotted overrides.

findings.title: aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax applied to native input[type="number"] — redundant and potentially conflicting
findings.description: These are ARIA range attributes appropriate for role="slider" or custom spinbuttons. A native <input type="number"> already exposes its value, min, and max via the accessibility tree through its implicit spinbutton role. Adding these ARIA attributes creates a mismatch. Screen readers may announce conflicting value information or ignore the ARIA overrides.
findings.fix: Remove aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax from the native <input type="number">. The native attributes (value, min, max) already communicate this information correctly to assistive technology.

findings.title: Missing aria-required on native number input
findings.description: The native <input type="number"> has ?required but no aria-required="true". Same shadow DOM AT reliability issue as B2-002 and B2-006.
findings.fix: Add aria-required=${this.required ? 'true' : nothing} to the native <input> element.

findings.title: No aria-label property — no accessible name fallback when label is omitted
findings.description: Unlike hx-text-input and hx-textarea, hx-number-input does not expose an ariaLabel / aria-label property. When the component is used without a label prop and without a slotted label, the native <input type="number"> inside the shadow DOM has no accessible name. Without an aria-label fallback property, there is no recovery path.
findings.fix: Add @property({ type: String, attribute: 'aria-label' }) override ariaLabel: string | null = null and pass it to the native input via aria-label=${ifDefined(this.ariaLabel || undefined)}. This matches the pattern established in hx-text-input.

findings.title: Error container uses role="status" instead of role="alert" — insufficient for error announcements
findings.description: The error container is assigned role="status" (an implicit polite live region). For validation errors, the ARIA APG recommends role="alert" (assertive) so the error is announced immediately. role="status" with aria-live="polite" can be delayed or preempted by other announcements, potentially causing the error to be missed in busy healthcare form contexts.
findings.fix: Change role="status" to role="alert" on the error container div.

findings.title: sm size variant checkbox box is 16x16px — below WCAG 2.5.5 touch target minimum
findings.description: The sm size variant sets the checkbox box to 1rem (16px). The surrounding label provides a larger clickable area, but the visual target does not meet the WCAG 2.5.5 recommendation of 44x44px for touch targets. In healthcare contexts (e.g., consent forms on tablets), this is a material barrier for users with motor impairments.
findings.fix: Apply min-height and min-width of 2.75rem (44px) to .checkbox__control for the sm variant, or add padding to the label to expand the touch target area without affecting the visual size of the checkbox box.

findings.title: Missing aria-required on native checkbox input
findings.description: The native <input type="checkbox"> uses ?required but lacks aria-required="true". Same shadow DOM AT reliability issue as B2-002, B2-006, B2-012.
findings.fix: Add aria-required=${this.required ? 'true' : nothing} to the native <input type="checkbox">.

findings.title: No helpText property — help text can only be provided via slot, with no aria-describedby association
findings.description: The component lacks a helpText @property. Consumers cannot provide help text via an attribute/property — only via the slot. More critically, the describedBy computation only includes this._helpTextId when this._hasHelpSlot is true. There is no mechanism for property-driven help text to be associated via aria-describedby, inconsistent with all other form components in the library.
findings.fix: Add @property({ type: String, attribute: 'help-text' }) helpText = '' and include this._helpTextId in describedBy when this._hasHelpSlot || !!this.helpText. Render the helpText property as fallback slot content, matching the pattern of hx-checkbox and hx-text-input.

findings.title: Empty legend renders when no label is provided — blank SR announcement
findings.description: The <legend> element is always rendered inside the <fieldset>, even when the label property is empty and no label slot content is provided. An empty <legend> is read by some screen readers as the group label, resulting in a blank announcement or awkward silence on NVDA/JAWS.
findings.fix: Conditionally render the <legend> only when label content is present. Check this.label || this._hasLabelSlot before rendering the legend wrapper.

findings.title: hx-radio host has role="radio" but no host-level keydown handler — Space key relies on event delegation that may fail
findings.description: hx-radio sets role="radio" and aria-checked on its host element. The roving tabindex pattern is managed by hx-radio-group, with focus landing on the hx-radio host. The SPACE key is handled by hx-radio-group's keydown handler via e.target.closest('hx-radio'). This will fail when focus is on a child element inside the shadow DOM. hx-radio has no @keydown handler on its own host, and the click handler is on the inner .radio div rather than the host — a synthesized click event from AT may not propagate to the inner div handler.
findings.fix: Add a @keydown handler directly on the hx-radio host for the Space key to dispatch hx-radio-select. Move the @click handler to :host or add a host-level click handler. Verify that synthesized AT click events land on the host and correctly activate the radio.

findings.title: hx-radio label not programmatically associated with the radio control
findings.description: The hx-radio component renders a .radio__label <span> containing the label text. The host has role="radio" and aria-checked, but no aria-labelledby pointing to the label span and no aria-label. The accessible name is computed from the host's subtree content — but Firefox and some JAWS versions do not compute accessible names from shadow DOM subtrees for custom elements with explicitly set ARIA roles. Radios may be announced with no accessible name.
findings.fix: Set this.setAttribute('aria-label', this.label) on the host in connectedCallback and updated() when label or slot content changes. For slotted label content, observe the slot and update aria-label accordingly. aria-labelledby cannot cross shadow DOM boundaries to reference the inner span.

findings.title: role="radiogroup" applied to native <fieldset> — overrides native group semantics
findings.description: The render output applies role="radiogroup" to the native <fieldset> element. A native fieldset has an implicit ARIA role of "group". Adding role="radiogroup" overrides the native semantics, causing the element to lose its native fieldset-legend association in some AT. The correct pattern is either a native <fieldset> (with implicit group role) or a <div role="radiogroup"> with explicit aria-labelledby.
findings.fix: Remove role="radiogroup" from the <fieldset>. The native fieldset with a <legend> and child radio elements provides the correct group semantics. If role="radiogroup" is required, use a <div role="radiogroup"> and replicate the legend/label via aria-labelledby.

findings.title: Slotted error content not associated with fieldset via aria-describedby
findings.description: The describedBy computation uses errorDescribedBy = !this._hasErrorSlot && hasError ? this._errorId : nothing. When the error slot IS populated (_hasErrorSlot = true), this evaluates to nothing, so the fieldset receives no aria-describedby reference to the error at all. Slotted error content is visible but not programmatically associated with the group — screen readers never announce it as the group error description.
findings.fix: When _hasErrorSlot is true, assign an ID to the slotted error element via the slot change handler and include that ID in aria-describedby. Alternatively, ensure the wrapper div always has the stable _errorId so aria-describedby continues to reference it regardless of whether content is prop-driven or slot-driven.

findings.title: sm size switch track is 32x18px — below WCAG 2.5.5 touch target minimum
findings.description: The sm size variant renders a switch track of approximately 32x18px (2rem x 1.125rem). WCAG 2.5.5 requires interactive touch targets to be at least 44x44 CSS pixels. In healthcare mobile contexts (tablet-based patient intake forms), users with motor impairments will have difficulty accurately activating the sm switch.
findings.fix: Add a minimum touch target to the sm size track button: min-width: 2.75rem; min-height: 2.75rem with the track visuals centered inside via padding. Alternatively, use a transparent padding pseudo-element to expand the clickable area without changing visual dimensions.

findings.title: Error container conditionally inserted — role="alert" may not fire in VoiceOver
findings.description: The error div with role="alert" is conditionally inserted (rendered only when hasError). VoiceOver on macOS requires the live region container to pre-exist in the DOM before text is populated.
findings.fix:
Keep the error container in the DOM at all times as a persistent live region:
${hasError ? this.error : ''}
.

findings.title: label[for] and aria-labelledby both point to the same label — potential double-announcement
findings.description: The switch renders a <label for="${buttonId}"> and also sets aria-labelledby pointing to the same label element's ID on the button. Having both mechanisms simultaneously can cause NVDA with Firefox to announce the label text twice when the switch receives focus.
findings.fix: Use only one labeling mechanism. Since both label and button are in the same shadow root, retain <label for> (the preferred native HTML approach) and remove aria-labelledby from the button. Alternatively, remove the for attribute from the label and retain aria-labelledby.

findings.title: No accessible name fallback when neither label property nor label slot is provided
findings.description: When no label or label slot is used, the input has aria-labelledby referencing undefined (ifDefined evaluates to nothing). There is no aria-label fallback property. A native <input type="range"> with no accessible name is announced only with its current value and role. In healthcare contexts (e.g., pain scale, medication dosage slider), an unnamed slider is a critical barrier.
findings.fix: Add @property({ type: String, attribute: 'aria-label' }) override ariaLabel: string | null = null and apply aria-label=${ifDefined(this.ariaLabel || undefined)} to the native input when hasLabel is false. Document that either label or aria-label is required.

findings.title: No error state or aria-invalid support — validation errors cannot be communicated to AT
findings.description: hx-slider has no error property, no aria-invalid, and no error announcement mechanism. In healthcare scenarios, sliders are used for numeric data entry (dosage, weight, pain scale). The component integrates with ElementInternals for form validity but provides no UI or AT mechanism to communicate invalid state to screen reader users.
findings.fix: Add an error property and an error message container with role="alert". Apply aria-invalid="true" to the native input when error is set. Include the error container ID in aria-describedby. This brings hx-slider into parity with all other form components.

findings.title: show-value display not connected to aria-describedby
findings.description: When the show-value attribute is present, the formatted current value is displayed visually but is not referenced in the native input's aria-describedby. Custom value formatting (units, labels) is not surfaced to assistive technology. Screen readers hear the raw value via aria-valuenow only.
findings.fix: Assign a stable ID to the value display element and include it in the native input's aria-describedby when show-value is active.

findings.title: Dropzone does not announce accepted file type or size constraints to assistive technology
findings.description: The dropzone has role="button" with aria-label set to the labelDropzone text only. When accept or maxSize constraints are configured, they are not included in the accessible name or description. Screen reader users cannot discover what file types are accepted or what the size limit is before attempting to upload — they encounter the error after the fact.
findings.fix: Add constraint information to the accessible description via aria-describedby pointing to a visually-present or sr-only element listing accepted file types and size limits. Compute the description string from the accept and maxSize properties.

findings.title: role="alert" and aria-live="polite" conflict on error container
findings.description: The error container has both role="alert" and aria-live="polite". The alert role carries an implicit aria-live="assertive" — applying aria-live="polite" alongside it creates contradictory live region semantics. Browsers resolve this inconsistently: some respect the role, others respect the explicit attribute. In a healthcare context, error messages must be reliably announced.
findings.fix: Remove aria-live="polite" from the error container. role="alert" alone provides aria-live="assertive" semantics, which is the correct urgency level for validation errors. If polite announcement is intentional, use role="status" with aria-live="polite" and remove role="alert".

findings.title: File validation errors dispatched via hx-error event but not auto-announced to AT
findings.description: When file validation fails (_processFiles detects wrong type or oversized file), an hx-error event is dispatched. However, there is no internal live region that auto-announces the validation error. A screen reader user who drops an invalid file receives no AT notification unless the consuming application manually handles hx-error and sets the error property.
findings.fix: Add an internal aria-live="assertive" region that is populated with the validation error message immediately when _processFiles detects an invalid file. This provides immediate AT notification independent of consumer event handling.

findings.title: File remove button touch target is approximately 22x22px — below WCAG 2.5.5 minimum
findings.description: The remove button (.file-item__remove) has padding: var(--hx-space-1, 0.25rem) — adding 4px on each side to a 14x14px SVG icon yields an approximate target of 22x22px. This is less than half the required 44x44px WCAG 2.5.5 minimum, creating a significant barrier for users with motor impairments.
findings.fix: Increase padding on .file-item__remove to at least 0.75rem on all sides, or set min-width: 2.75rem and min-height: 2.75rem to ensure the touch target meets the 44x44px minimum.
